I can step in due to my profession.

First thing you really need to ask yourself is the question What Do I Want To Do With The Phone?

Simply put, if you're a social media type, you'll want something with a decent set of cameras (front and back), a fair amount of storage space (8GB and up) and you definitely want expandable storage if you can get it. If you're a gamer, you'll want something with a really good screen, good cameras (as some games do augmented reality), and lots of onboard storage as some of these games can take up a full gig or two of space. If you're more of a productivity type...you get the picture.

Next, what is your tech level? If you are confident enough, you can get an android based phone for it's customization. You can also root (hack) your phone and overclock the processor if you're really confident. If you're a first-timer and not too sure what you want to do, perhaps an iPhone may be something you'll want because iPhones all run pretty much the same way. They do have a level of customization but not quite to the degree of Android. Windows phones can be a little buggy but keep in mind I am basing this on my use and I've only ever used one Windows phone. Incidentally, it won't download and install apps now because the thing's just outdated hardware.

Now, here's the clincher. How Much Can You Spend On The Phone? and What's your price range per month? This one is important but it's last because you can now make adjustments to the first two based on the selection at hand.

Example: I left AT&T because my employee plan was coming to an end. I had a Samsung Galaxy S4 at the time. Great phone and can't really tell you how great it was because it was forever evolving in apps that I used, kept, discarded and even fell under running water in a sink for a full 45 seconds before I realized it. Never hurt it though. That thing went strong for over a year before my sweet deal was coming to an end. I decided I didn't want to pay too much more so I looked into prepaid. Boost had the best deal going. For another ten bucks a month ($45 per month) and I could well over double my data (5GB at high-speed). I sacrificed half of my onboard stoage going from 16GB to 8GB and picked up an LG Volt. Great phone, still have it but I upgraded it a few months later to the LG G Stylo which is similar to a Galaxy Note in size and a little smoother in operation. I have few complaints with both phones and I pay less than 50 per month. Despite the sacrifice in storage it was still win-win.

As you can see, it's all very personalized. I recommend any phone with Android on them because, after using Blackberry, iPhone, Windows Phone and Android, Android just felt right to me.

My advice is read reviews, look at different phones, look into different carriers and if you need any help, just inbox me. Always happy to help.

Exactly what the title says. I've sustained multiple injuries to both ankles. The most recent was about 13 months ago and it's still moderately swollen and intermittently painful. Even after physical therapy it hasn't fully healed. I haven't been able to work out for a while and I'm going crazy. I plan to start again tomorrow. But I don't want to skip legs constantly. I know a few machines I can do for them, buy I'm looking for some variety so I can work all the muscle groups.

Thanks!
Injured ankles. Can't squat, deadlift, etc. Even yoga for longer than 20 minutes hurts. What exercises can I do for legs? What exercises can I do to strengthen the weak ankles?

Honestly? I know it's not what your looking for, but you should express your concerns to your PT. You shouldn't try to get on it before it's ready because you risk re-injuring yourself which would put you out of commission for longer :/

The only three I can think of that don't tax the ankle are leg curls, leg extensions and leg kickbacks. I don't think you can hit every muscle in the leg without planting your feet though. I had a bad sprained ankle 5 years ago that still bothers me a few times a year. It sucks but don't let it discourage you. Even if you just do those three exercises, its way better than not training your lower body at all.

If you can't do an exercise for 20 minutes, do it for 15.

Can you peddle a bike?

Work the body parts you can, test the body parts you can't every other month and consult a physician.

Try some variations on leg lifts or air cycling to work your legs or core. You really need to see another PT about your ankles though, and invest in a good brace. My SO tore his tendon and this ankle brace works amazingly, even for intense running.

You need to define your goal.

If you want to have an ankle that works properly later in life, the smart thing do to would be to let that fucker heal until it's not swollen. Unless you have some medical disorder causing poor blood circulation you shouldn't have a sprained ankle that is swollen after a year. To start do your inside, outside, and around work with the bands your pt should've given you to do at home. If you didn't get them, but some. ACTUALLY DO THEM! Many people skip it when they go home and reinjure that fucker (Hello 16 year old invincible me.) LIGHT work standing on the bosu ball after that while holding the wall. Then branch out with simple body weight exercises or light swimming. It all starts b building your range of motion and those small stabilizing muscles. IF YOU DO NOT BUILD UP YOUR ROM AND STABILIZATION MUSCLES FIRST YOU WILL KEEP HURTING YOUR ANKLE AGAIN!

It sounds like when you mention "skipping leg day" you're going for mass on legs as to not look disproportionate? If aesthetics is the goal, volume is key. Leg curls, leg extensions, hip abductor machine (both ways) are your best bet. Do TONS of them mixing pause sets, drop sets, burnouts, whatever you can think of because they're all you have. Also, do the other stuff anyways so you can walk when you turn 60.

Obviously this is just internet advice, but try to improve the flexibility through your entire legs. Your ankles may hurt, but it could be having knock on effects through the rest of you legs. Can you touch you toes? Can you put your head to your knees? Can you do the splits? Are your calves flexible? Loosening up all the supporting muscles around your ankles will help as well. Don't underestimate the power of stretching, especially as you age.

I've broken 1 ankle, and rolled both of them a number of times. I have since become much more focused on flexibility in addition to strength.
